column1: Pheidole dentata, a native ant of the south-eastern U.S., isn’t immortal.
column2: 齿大头蚁（Pheidole dentata）是美国东南部的本土蚁种，它并非长生不死。

column1: But scientists have found that it doesn’t seem to show any signs of aging.
column2: 但科学家发现，这种蚂蚁似乎并没有出现任何衰老的迹象。
column5: show any signs of|表现出任何……的迹象

column1: Old worker ants can do everything just as well as the youngsters, and their brains appear just as sharp.
column2: 年老的工蚁样样都能做得和年轻工蚁一样好，头脑似乎也同样敏锐。
column4: just as well as|做得和……一样好

column1: ‘We get a picture that these ants really don’t decline,’ says Ysabel Giraldo, who studied the ants for her doctoral thesis at Boston University.
column2: “据我们观察，这些蚂蚁的机能确实没有衰退。”伊莎贝尔·希拉尔多说。她在波士顿大学攻读博士期间，为撰写学位论文研究了这些蚂蚁。
column3: get a picture|形成一种认识

column1: Such age-defying feats are rare in the animal kingdom.
column2: 这样仿佛能抵抗衰老的本领，在动物界并不多见。

column1: Naked mole rats can live for almost 30 years and stay fit for nearly their entire lives.
column2: 裸鼹鼠能活将近30年，而且几乎一辈子都身体康健。
column6: nearly their entire lives|几乎整个一生

column1: They can still reproduce even when old, and they never get cancer.
column2: 它们直至年老仍能繁殖，而且从来不会得癌症。

column1: But the vast majority of animals deteriorate with age just like people do.
column2: 但绝大多数动物都和人一样，身体会随着年龄增长而衰退。

column1: Like the naked mole rat, ants are social creatures that usually live in highly organised colonies.
column2: 与裸鼹鼠一样，蚂蚁也是社会性动物，通常生活在组织严密的群体中。

column1: ‘It’s this social complexity that makes P. dentata useful for studying aging in people,’ says Giraldo, now at the California Institute of Technology.
column2: “正是这种复杂的社会生活，让齿大头蚁成为研究人类衰老的好对象。”如今任职于加州理工学院的希拉尔多说。
column3: social complexity|社会生活的复杂性
column7: California Institute of Technology|加州理工学院

column1: Humans are also highly social, a trait that has been connected to healthier aging.
column2: 人类也具有很强的社会性，而这种特征被认为与更健康地步入老年有关。
column6: healthier aging|更健康的老龄过程

column1: By contrast, most animal studies of aging use mice, worms or fruit flies, which all lead much more isolated lives.
column2: 相比之下，大多数关于衰老的动物研究选用小鼠、蠕虫或果蝇，这些动物的生活都要孤立得多。
column8: isolated lives|彼此较少联系的生活

column1: In the lab, P. dentata worker ants typically live for around 140 days.
column2: 在实验室里，齿大头蚁的工蚁通常能活约140天。

column1: Giraldo focused on ants at four age ranges: 20 to 22 days, 45 to 47 days, 95 to 97 days and 120 to 122 days.
column2: 希拉尔多重点观察了四个日龄段的蚂蚁：20至22天、45至47天、95至97天，以及120至122天。

column1: Unlike all previous studies, which only estimated how old the ants were, her work tracked the ants from the time the pupae became adults, so she knew their exact ages.
column2: 以往的研究都只是估计蚂蚁的年龄。希拉尔多则从蚂蚁由蛹羽化为成虫时就开始追踪，所以知道每只蚂蚁的确切日龄。

column1: Then she put them through a range of tests.
column2: 接下来，她让这些蚂蚁接受了一系列测试。

column1: Giraldo watched how well the ants took care of the young of the colony, recording how often each ant attended to, carried and fed them.
column2: 希拉尔多观察工蚁照顾群体幼蚁的能力，记录每只工蚁照料、搬运和喂养幼蚁的频率。

column1: She compared how well 20-day-old and 95-day-old ants followed the telltale scent that the insects usually leave to mark a trail to food.
column2: 蚂蚁通常会留下特有的气味，标出通往食物的路径。她比较了20日龄和95日龄工蚁追踪这种气味的本领。
column6: telltale scent|能指明踪迹的气味
column7: mark a trail|标出一条路径

column1: She tested how ants responded to light and also measured how active they were by counting how often ants in a small dish walked across a line.
column2: 她测试蚂蚁对光的反应，还数了数它们在小碟里越过一条线的次数，以此衡量它们的活跃程度。

column1: And she experimented with how ants react to live prey: a tethered fruit fly.
column2: 她还用一只拴住的果蝇做实验，观察蚂蚁对活猎物有什么反应。

column1: Giraldo expected the older ants to perform poorly in all these tasks.
column2: 希拉尔多原以为，年老工蚁在所有这些任务中的表现都会很差。

column1: But the elderly insects were all good caretakers and trail-followers—the 95-day-old ants could track the scent even longer than their younger counterparts.
column2: 可是，年老的工蚁个个都很会照顾幼蚁，也擅长循迹。95日龄工蚁甚至能比年轻同伴更长时间地追踪气味。

column1: They all responded to light well, and the older ants were more active.
column2: 各年龄组的工蚁对光的反应都很好，年老工蚁甚至更活跃。

column1: And when it came to reacting to prey, the older ants attacked the poor fruit fly just as aggressively as the young ones did, flaring their mandibles or pulling at the fly’s legs.
column2: 在对猎物的反应方面，年老工蚁和年轻工蚁一样凶猛，都狠扑那只可怜的果蝇，有的张开大颚，有的拖拽果蝇的腿。

column1: Then Giraldo compared the brains of 20-day-old and 95-day-old ants, identifying any cells that were close to death.
column2: 接着，希拉尔多比较了20日龄与95日龄工蚁的脑，辨认出其中哪些细胞正接近死亡。

column1: She saw no major differences with age, nor was there any difference in the location of the dying cells, showing that age didn’t seem to affect specific brain functions.
column2: 她没有看到不同日龄之间存在明显差异，濒死细胞出现的位置也没有差别。这表明，年龄似乎并未影响特定的脑功能。

column1: Ants and other insects have structures in their brains called mushroom bodies, which are important for processing information, learning and memory.
column2: 蚂蚁和其他昆虫的脑内有一种称为蕈形体的结构，它在信息处理、学习和记忆中起着重要作用。

column1: She also wanted to see if aging affects the density of synaptic complexes within these structures—regions where neurons come together.
column2: 她还想看看衰老会不会影响这些结构中突触复合体的密度。突触复合体就是神经元相互连接的区域。

column1: Again, the answer was no.
column2: 结果同样是否定的。

column1: What was more, the old ants didn’t experience any drop in the levels of either serotonin or dopamine—brain chemicals whose decline often coincides with aging.
column2: 不止如此，老龄工蚁体内的血清素和多巴胺水平都没有下降。通常情况下，这两种脑内化学物质的减少都与衰老同时发生。
column4: drop in the levels|水平下降

column1: In humans, for example, a decrease in serotonin has been linked to Alzheimer’s disease.
column2: 以人类为例，血清素减少与阿尔茨海默病之间存在关联。

column1: ‘This is the first time anyone has looked at both behavioral and neural changes in these ants so thoroughly,’ says Giraldo, who recently published the findings in the Proceedings of the Royal Society B.
column2: “这是第一次有人把这些蚂蚁在行为和神经方面的变化都研究得如此透彻。”希拉尔多说。她最近已将研究结果发表在《英国皇家学会学报B辑》上。
column8: Proceedings of the Royal Society B|《英国皇家学会学报B辑》

column1: Scientists have looked at some similar aspects in bees, but the results of recent bee studies were mixed—some studies showed age-related declines, which biologists call senescence, and others didn’t.
column2: 科学家也研究过蜜蜂的某些类似特征，但近期有关蜜蜂的研究得出的结果并不一致。有些研究观察到了随年龄增长而发生的机能衰退，生物学家称之为衰老，有些则没有。
column6: age-related declines|与年龄有关的机能衰退

column1: ‘For now, the study raises more questions than it answers,’ Giraldo says, ‘including how P. dentata stays in such good shape.’
column2: “目前，这项研究提出的问题比它回答的还多，”希拉尔多说，“其中一个就是齿大头蚁究竟是怎样一直保持这么好的状态的。”
column4: raises more questions|提出更多问题
column7: in such good shape|处在这么好的状态

column1: Also, if the ants don’t deteriorate with age, why do they die at all?
column2: 还有，如果这些蚂蚁的机能不随年龄增长而衰退，它们究竟为什么还会死呢？

column1: Out in the wild, the ants probably don’t live for a full 140 days thanks to predators, disease and just being in an environment that’s much harsher than the comforts of the lab.
column2: 在野外，受到天敌、疾病等因素的影响，加之生存环境远比实验室恶劣，这些蚂蚁恐怕活不满140天。

column1: ‘The lucky ants that do live into old age may suffer a steep decline just before dying,’ Giraldo says, but she can’t say for sure because her study wasn’t designed to follow an ant’s final moments.
column2: “那些有幸活到老年的蚂蚁，可能会在临死前才迅速衰弱。”希拉尔多说。但她还不能确定，因为这项研究原本就没有打算跟踪蚂蚁生命的最后时刻。
column3: live into old age|活到老年

column1: ‘It will be important to extend these findings to other species of social insects,’ says Gene E. Robinson, an entomologist at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign.
column2: “还应把这些研究结果推广到其他社会性昆虫中去检验，这一点很重要。”伊利诺伊大学厄巴纳-香槟分校的昆虫学家吉恩·罗宾逊说。
column3: extend these findings|将这些研究结果推广
column7: University of Illinois|伊利诺伊大学

column1: This ant might be unique, or it might represent a broader pattern among other social bugs with possible clues to the science of aging in larger animals.
column2: 齿大头蚁或许是个特例，也可能代表其他社会性昆虫中更普遍的规律，并为研究较大型动物的衰老提供线索。

column1: Either way, it seems that for these ants, age really doesn’t matter.
column2: 无论是哪一种情况，对于这些蚂蚁来说，年龄似乎真的没什么影响。
column6: doesn’t matter|不重要，没什么影响
